title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement a new generation of gender-responsive national employment policies, including for youth

description.narrative:
In February 2021, the Council of Ministers approved the Revised Employment Policy Implementation Plan covering the period 2021-2024. This plan has a major stake in the pro-employment budget, as well as promotion of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) issues, in the face of prevention measures for COVID-19 or other similar diseases. The preparation of the revised National Employment Policy (NEP) Implementation Plan was led by the SEJE (Secretariat of State for Youth and Employment), in collaboration with the ILO and other sectoral ministries like the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Public Works. With support from the Government of Sweden, in May 2021, the ILO convened a high-level meeting on employment, attended by 180 participants, including government leaders, youth associations, higher education representatives, international organizations, civil society, media and business. The meeting was opened by His Excellency Prime Minister with interventions from various institutions, namely: National Youth Council, Labour Organization, Confederation of Economic Associations, ILO and the Secretary of State for Youth and Employment. The meeting was an opportunity to discuss the actions contained in the NEP Action Plan as well as other sectoral plans that are being implemented, which also contribute to the promotion of employment and employability, with emphasis on the following: 1) The Industrial Policy and Strategy; 2) The Aquaculture Development Strategy; 3) The Investment Law Regulation; and 4) The Project Sustenta, with great impact on agriculture.
The ILO also prepared two key reports to provide additional tools to SEJE in defining policies and strategies for employment promotion: 1) Final report on pro-employment budgeting; and 2) COVID-19 and employment: pro-employment policy options for Mozambique. In July 2021, the ILO in coordination with SEJE, organized a technical follow up meeting to discuss the recommendations and implementation of interventions from the high-level meeting.

Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
In June 2021, the Government of Mozambique, through the National Road Administration (ANE), adopted the employment intensive investment approach to repair and reconstruction cyclone damaged rural infrastructure including access roads and environmental protection work to implement the national Employment Policy. ANE implemented pro-employment projects incorporating decent work measures including fair labour standards, equal opportunities for men and women as well as occupational safety and health. The ANE, as an institution responsible for the development and maintenance of all classified roads in Mozambique, developed employment intensive training capabilities under its Road Training Center (CFE), benefitting ANE staff, municipalities, government districts, private sector (contractors) and workers.
The Government of Mozambique repaired and reconstructed rural roads using pro-employment, climate smart and Build-Back–Better principles and approaches as part of rolling out the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP). With support from the Government of Japan, the ILO provided technical and managerial training on the employment intensive approach benefiting 75 unemployed young women, men and other vulnerable groups, 6 small scale contractors from the private sector, and 24 engineers and technicians from ANE, CFE and municipalities.
The ILO supported the planning, implementation and monitoring of the delivery of quality infrastructures, especially tertiary roads that connect isolated rural communities to markets, contributing towards the rebuilding of livelihoods through increased opportunities for accessing markets and jobs.
Climate-smart building techniques were adopted with the aim of building the resilience and coping mechanism for communities in Vanduzi district by building capacities for local workers to enable municipalities and districts to restore rural infrastructure and increasing their resilience against future shocks using the ILO's labour-based approach.
ILO ensured the inclusion of rights-based approach in the delivery of public programmes incorporating Gender equality (with minimum women participation pegged at 30%), fair working conditions, OSH as well as community participation in decision making through upgrading and maintenance of roads.
